Messages.Author: s...@dolnet.gr
Messages.Body:
As a new player to VTES, i have to say that although is a great game it
has its flaws...like many revised rules, cards errata (seems that never
stop), and many other things that bring confusion at the moment of play.
One major flaw is that the owner of most cards and expansions (any
kind), has more choices and can construct a more powerfull deck to oust
his/her opponents.Me and my friends are trying to play not allowing
duplicate cards of any kind.We will see how it is gonna be.
We also wish to see a new cardgame with Highlander thematology.It will
be nice for my friends.
And a question: is it possible to be blocked by more than one
Methuselah, meaning that the combat that will occure, have more than 2
minions participate at the same time?
Thanks in advance.

Messages.Author: James Hamblin
Messages.Body:
s...@dolnet.gr wrote:
>
> As a new player to VTES, i have to say that although is a great game it
> has its flaws...like many revised rules,

Well, the rules are fairly complex, and they did a horrible job with the
rulebook, so revisions are unfortunately necessary.

> cards errata (seems that never
> stop),

One drawback of complex rules is that sometimes cards interact in a way
never intended. Mostly, though, the eratta makes intuitive sense.

> and many other things that bring confusion at the moment of play.
> One major flaw is that the owner of most cards and expansions (any
> kind), has more choices and can construct a more powerfull deck to oust
> his/her opponents.

Not true. The "money makes the deck better" syndrome plaguing most
CCG's is, for the most part, avoided by Jyhad. Most of the useful cards
are common, and boxes of boosters sell for around $20.

> Me and my friends are trying to play not allowing

> duplicate cards of any kind. We will see how it is gonna be.

Four card limit is bad enough. One card limit would be horrible. My
advice is to have your group pitch in for a couple of boxes ($10 for ~18
boosters is a great deal) and get the cards you need.

> We also wish to see a new cardgame with Highlander thematology. It will

> be nice for my friends.

Hmmm... Well, fat chance getting this from Wizards. They seem to want
to spend all year stuffing the cash cow.

> And a question: is it possible to be blocked by more than one
> Methuselah, meaning that the combat that will occure, have more than 2
> minions participate at the same time?

No. There's a particular order that players choose to block, though
usually you use gentlemanly rules; "Oh, you wanted to block that, too?
OK, go ahead." or "Oh, I didn't see that you also had +1 intercept, but
I really wanted to block this. Thanks. I'll do you a solid later."

Have fun!

James

Messages.Author: Robert Goudie
Messages.Body:
s...@dolnet.gr wrote:
>
[clip]

> One major flaw is that the owner of most cards and expansions (any
> kind), has more choices and can construct a more powerfull deck to oust

> his/her opponents.Me and my friends are trying to play not allowing
> duplicate cards of any kind.We will see how it is gonna be.

Some of what you say is certainly true, though it was never meant to be
this way. Most cards in the original Jyhad set could be countered with
other common cards. Generally speaking, having the most cards didn't
mean you'd win more.

Some of the new cards such as the Tomb of Ramses has wrecked my life
many times and I don't have enough of my own to level the playing field.

I don't think that your 1 card limit will make the game more enjoyable
for you though. It is impossible to build a cohesive deck strategy that
way.

Maybe you should allow the free proxying of cards. Everyone gets
sleeves and you can have as many of any card as you want. The playing
field is then
leveled.

And no, only one block may occur.

Robert

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
s...@dolnet.gr wrote:
> And a question: is it possible to be blocked by more than one
> Methuselah, meaning that the combat that will occure, have more than 2
> minions participate at the same time?

No. Once a blocker succeeds in blocking the action (i.e., the
blocker has enough intercept to match the acting minion's stealth,
and the blocker is not otherwise prevented from blocking), then
the action is completed (fails) and combat occurs.

No one else can attempt to block at this point, because their is
no action to block. The action ended when the first block was
successful.
